subject: HorizonX elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation in progress and recovery commitments
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alan Rogers <alan.rogers@stellar.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: HorizonX elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation in progress and recovery commitments

Hi Alan —

Quick note to let you know we observed an elevated rate of 5xx and timeout errors originating from the HorizonX generator model cluster starting ~08:50 PDT this morning. Impact appears focused on your /v1/generate and chat endpoints that pin HorizonX or use the default routing policy.

What we see so far: 
- Error spike: 5xx rate from HorizonX instances rose to ~18% of requests at peak (normally <0.2%).
- Timeouts: tail latency increased, with the 95th moving from ~320ms to ~2.4s.
- Affected traffic slice: ~25% of StellarAI production tokens during the window.

Immediate actions (already taken):
- Failover: we triggered policy-based fallbacks to rw-horizon-lite for the highest-latency requests to keep responses flowing.
- Scaling: we automatically increased HorizonX replica count and spun up warm instances in the same region.
- Routing: we diverted new requests to dedicated capacity pools where possible to reduce cross-tenant noise.

Attachments: small sample of error traces (horizonx-error-sample.log) and the initial timeline (horizonx-timeline-20270611.csv).

Next steps from our side: 
- Karthik and the infra team are performing targeted triage to identify root cause; we expect a preliminary update within 3–4 hours.
- We’ll keep your on-call ops looped; if you prefer a short sync, we can hop on a 15m call in ~30 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your customers. We’ll prioritize stability and keep you updated frequently.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: HorizonX elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation in progress and recovery commitments

Alan —

Thanks for the quick reply and for the sample IDs. Two quick answers up front: 
- Billing semantics: fallback responses to rw-horizon-lite are billed at the fallback model's rate; we logged which requests were routed and will provide a reconciliation export you can feed into billing.
- ETA: We performed a rollback to HorizonX v2.7 (previous stable) at ~12:40 PDT and observed error rates drop to baseline by ~12:58 PDT. We are closely monitoring to ensure no recurrence during the afternoon.

Preliminary root cause (triage update from infra): 
- We observed a regression in a low-level quantized attention kernel introduced in the v2.8 rollout that occasionally caused memory fragmentation on longer-context requests. The fragmentation yielded transient OOMs and subsequent 5xx responses, primarily for sequences >2k tokens.
- The rollout triggered small memory pressure spikes across the HorizonX pool which, compounded by a specific traffic pattern from a partner bucket, amplified the error surface.

Actions completed: 
- Rolled back to v2.7 (stable).
- Temporarily increased replica headroom and disabled the kernel variant while engineering prepares a safe patch.
- Issued routing fallbacks and warmed fallback instances to absorb traffic.

Planned next steps: 
- Engineering will validate a patched kernel with extended long-context test vectors; target for a controlled re-roll is 48–72 hours after validation.
- We'll generate a reconciliation file showing which request-ids were billed against fallback vs HorizonX and share it by EOD.
- Postmortem: drafting a full RCA with timeline and mitigations; we'll share a first draft tomorrow and schedule a readout if you'd like.

Cc'ing Karthik and Marissa for visibility. If you want an interim status call I can be available at 14:00 PDT.

—
Naomi

Subject: HorizonX incident closure: RCA summary & next steps

Alan —

Follow-up with the promised summary and next steps now that we've stabilized HorizonX. Thanks again for the samples and for the patience from the StellarAI team.

Incident summary (brief): 
- Window: 2027-06-11T08:50:00–2027-06-11T12:58:00 PDT (peak at ~09:30).
- Symptom: elevated 5xx rate and long-tail timeouts from HorizonX instances serving long-context requests.
- Root cause: regression in a quantized attention kernel rolled in v2.8 causing intermittent memory fragmentation/OOMs on sequences >2k tokens; coupled with a concentrated traffic pattern from a partner bucket which amplified failure rates.

Immediate remediation: rollback to v2.7, disabled the kernel variant, increased replica headroom, and routed fallback traffic to rw-horizon-lite. Error rates returned to baseline within ~18 minutes of the rollback.

What we’re doing to prevent recurrence: 
- Patch & test: engineering has a patch to the attention kernel; it is undergoing long-context stress tests and synthetic replay of partner traffic.
- Canary plan: safe canary rollout with traffic shaping and preflight mem/profiler checks (will take place with a narrow time window and daytime monitoring).
- Monitoring: added a new long-context memory pressure alert and higher-fidelity histogram of per-sequence allocation to catch regressions earlier.
- Communication: we will share the postmortem doc (postmortem-draft.md) and a reconciliation CSV showing which requests were routed to fallback vs HorizonX and associated billing implications.

Compensation/credits: we will provide a one-time credit for the traffic affected by the degraded window while we finalize the reconciliation — we’ll confirm numbers after the billing export completes.

Attachments & links: postmortem draft attached and read-only copy on Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HorizonX-RCA. HubSpot link with incident and deal context: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-5732.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30m RCA readout next week with engineering and product owners; please share preferred times and I'll coordinate.

Thanks again — we take incidents like this seriously and appreciate the partnership as we shore up long-context stability.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
